paragraphs.title: The Idolatrous Elders and God's Answer

answers: Certain of the elders of Israel
easy.explanation: Verse 1 says that certain of the elders of Israel came and sat before Ezekiel.
easy.q: Who came and sat before Ezekiel?

easy.explanation: The Lord said that these men had set up their idols in their hearts.
easy.q: What had the elders set up in their hearts?

easy.explanation: The passage reveals that the Lord knew they had idols in their hearts and had turned away from Him.
easy.q: What did the Lord know about the elders?

answers: Because they refused to sit down
Because they held idols in their hearts
Because they did not know Ezekiel
medium.explanation: Although they came to the prophet, they continued to cling to their idols and iniquity.
medium.q: Why was God's answer to the elders connected with rebuke and judgment?

answers: The sinful thing that caused them to fall
medium.explanation: Their iniquity was like a stumblingblock placed before them.
medium.q: What does the phrase “the stumblingblock of their iniquity” describe?

answers: They came only to hear a story
They sought God outwardly while still clinging to sin
medium.explanation: Their outward visit to the prophet did not match the idolatry in their hearts.
medium.q: What inconsistency is shown by the elders coming to the prophet while keeping their idols?

answers: Their inward estrangement from God through idols
Their refusal to sit before Ezekiel
challenge.explanation: The elders were estranged from the Lord through the idols they had set up in their hearts.
challenge.q: What central sin did the Lord expose in the elders?

answers: The Lord did not know their condition
The Lord would answer while exposing and judging their sin
The Lord promised to grant their request
challenge.explanation: God's response would not ignore their sin but would reveal and judge it.
challenge.q: What does “should I be enquired of at all by them?” imply in this passage?

answers: The idols revealed their inward turning away from God
The idols proved their faithfulness to God
There was no relationship between the heart and conduct
challenge.explanation: Their inward idolatry showed that they had become estranged from the Lord.
challenge.q: What relationship exists between the idols in their hearts and their conduct?

short_answers.question: Where did the elders sit when they came to Ezekiel?
short_answers.explanation: Verse 1 says they came and sat before Ezekiel.

short_answers.question: What did the elders put before their faces?
short_answers.explanation: Verse 3 says they put the stumblingblock of their iniquity before their faces.

short_answers.question: Through what were the elders estranged from God?
short_answers.explanation: Verse 5 says they were estranged from the Lord through their idols.

paragraphs.title: The Call to Repentance and the Judgment of Sinner and Prophet

easy.explanation: The Lord commanded Israel to repent, turn from their idols, and turn away from their abominations.
easy.q: What did the house of Israel have to turn away from?

answers: Anyone of Israel and the stranger dwelling in Israel
easy.explanation: The warning included every person of Israel and the stranger who sojourned in Israel.
easy.q: Who was included in the warning of verse 7?

answers: The Lord would destroy him from among His people
easy.explanation: The Lord said He would stretch out His hand against such a prophet and destroy him from Israel.
easy.q: What would happen to a prophet who was deceived and spoke a false thing?

answers: Removing idols and turning away from abominations
medium.explanation: Repentance required turning from idols and abominations.
medium.q: What was required before a person could rightly turn to God?

medium.explanation: The person described had separated himself from the Lord.
medium.q: What does the KJV word “separateth” mean in this context?

answers: Both had failed to remain faithful to God
medium.explanation: The sinner clung to idols, while the deceived prophet spoke falsely; both bore punishment.
medium.q: Why were both the sinful person and the prophet held responsible?

answers: To increase the number of idols
To keep Israel from going astray and restore them as God's people
To replace the prophet with a king
challenge.explanation: The stated purpose was that Israel would go no more astray and would be God's people.
challenge.q: What was the purpose of the judgment described in verses 8–11?

answers: Both the sinner and the prophet were accountable
The sinner was excused if the prophet spoke
challenge.explanation: Verse 10 gives both the prophet and the person seeking him the punishment of their iniquity.
challenge.q: What does the comparison between the punishment of the prophet and the punishment of the seeker teach?

answers: He sought God while still holding idols in his heart
He abandoned idols and fled from the prophet
He obeyed every word of the Lord
challenge.explanation: The person came to enquire of God but continued to place idols and sin before him.
challenge.q: What practical contradiction is shown by the person who came to enquire of the Lord?

short_answers.question: What command did the Lord give to the house of Israel?
short_answers.answer: Repent and turn from their idols.
short_answers.explanation: Verse 6 calls Israel to repent and turn away from its idols and abominations.

short_answers.question: What would the Lord set against the sinful man?
short_answers.explanation: Verse 8 says, “I will set my face against that man.”

short_answers.question: What did God desire Israel to become?
short_answers.explanation: Verse 11 says that Israel might be God's people and He might be their God.

paragraphs.title: The Four Calamities and the Limits of Personal Righteousness

easy.explanation: The Lord said He would break the staff of bread and send famine upon the land.
easy.q: What punishment would come upon a sinful land in verse 13?

easy.explanation: The passage names Noah, Daniel, and Job.
easy.q: Which three righteous men are named in the passage?

easy.explanation: The repeated statement says they would deliver only their own souls.
easy.q: What would these three men deliver by their righteousness?

answers: Famine, wild beasts, the sword, and pestilence
medium.explanation: The four judgments are famine, noisome beasts, the sword, and pestilence.
medium.q: What four judgments are described in the passage?

medium.explanation: Breaking the staff of bread describes removing the support of food and bringing famine.
medium.q: What does “the staff of the bread thereof” represent?

answers: The cutting off of man and beast
medium.explanation: The judgments repeatedly result in man and beast being cut off from the land.
medium.q: What common result would the judgments bring upon the land?

answers: A person's righteousness does not automatically save the land or other people
Many righteous people could certainly save the land
challenge.explanation: Even these three men would deliver only themselves by their righteousness.
challenge.q: What does the repeated mention of the three righteous men teach?

answers: The men would save their children but not the land
The men would be delivered, but their sons and daughters would not be delivered through them
No one could ever be delivered
challenge.explanation: The passage specifically says that sons and daughters would not be delivered by their righteousness.
challenge.q: What is the distinction between the salvation of the righteous men and that of their children?

answers: To show that even exemplary righteousness would not cancel the general judgment
To teach that they caused the calamities
To prove that they were kings of Jerusalem
challenge.explanation: Their example emphasizes that the judgment would remain, while they themselves alone would be delivered.
challenge.q: Why are Noah, Daniel, and Job mentioned in connection with all four judgments?

short_answers.question: What would the Lord break when sending famine?
short_answers.answer: The staff of the bread of the land.
short_answers.explanation: Verse 13 says the Lord would break the staff of the bread thereof.

short_answers.question: Name the three righteous men in the passage.
short_answers.explanation: These three men are named repeatedly in verses 14–20.

short_answers.question: What would the righteous men deliver?
short_answers.explanation: The passage says they would deliver only their own souls by their righteousness.

paragraphs.title: Jerusalem, the Survivors, and the Justice of Judgment

easy.explanation: Verse 21 says the four sore judgments would be sent upon Jerusalem.
easy.q: Against which city would the four judgments be sent?

easy.explanation: The passage says that a remnant of sons and daughters would be left.
easy.q: Who would remain as a remnant after the destruction?

easy.explanation: The survivors would come to the exiles, who would see their way and their doings.
easy.q: What would the exiles see in the survivors?

answers: Seeing the way and doings of the survivors
medium.explanation: The conduct of the survivors would help the exiles understand the reason for the judgment.
medium.q: What would comfort the exiles concerning the evil brought upon Jerusalem?

medium.explanation: The remnant is the portion left alive after the destruction.
medium.q: What does the word “remnant” mean in this passage?

answers: The destruction was justified and not done without cause
The survivors were responsible for everyone's exile
medium.explanation: They would know that the Lord had not done all He had done in Jerusalem without cause.
medium.q: What conclusion would the exiles reach after seeing the survivors?

answers: Their ways and doings would reflect the sins of Jerusalem
They would explain that the city had been wealthy
challenge.explanation: Seeing their ways and doings would help the exiles understand why judgment had come.
challenge.q: Why would the conduct of the survivors help establish the justice of the judgment?

answers: The remnant remains after the judgment and confirms its justice
The remnant proves that no destruction occurred
challenge.explanation: Survivors remain, but their conduct shows that the destruction was not without cause.
challenge.q: What is the relationship between the remnant and the destruction?

answers: The destruction was arbitrary, though some survived
The destruction and the survivors together testify to the justice of God's judgment
All Jerusalem was saved because of the survivors
challenge.explanation: The remnant does not cancel the judgment; it helps the exiles recognize its justice.
challenge.q: What idea best summarizes the final verses?

short_answers.question: What four judgments would come upon Jerusalem?
short_answers.answer: The sword, famine, noisome beasts, and pestilence.
short_answers.explanation: Verse 21 names these four sore judgments.

short_answers.question: Who would be left as a remnant?
short_answers.explanation: Verse 22 says that a remnant of sons and daughters would be brought forth.

short_answers.question: What would the exiles know after seeing the survivors' ways and doings?
short_answers.answer: That the Lord had not acted without cause.
short_answers.explanation: Verse 23 says they would know that God had not done all He had done without cause.
